newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher amid firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher amid firmer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open slightly higher Friday after a stronger ACCESS session and early talk of firmer cash prices, industry sources said.
July over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.19 to $2.20 after settling Thursday at $2.177 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, July last traded 3.2 cents higher at $2.209, edging past $2.20, which was earlier pegged as next resistance.
Early cash prices at Henry Hub were talked at $2.19-2.21.
Technical traders pegged resistance in July at $2.25, and then at $2.37 and the contract high of $2.44. Support was seen at $2.10, with the stronger backstop pegged at $2.08.

In Thursday's cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped one to two cents to the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes were down a similar amount to about $2.01, while New York city gate prices fell a few cents to the high-$2.30s.

Cooler-than-normal weather is expected to continue throughout most of the U.S. through this weekend, but forecasters are calling for the arrival of warmer air by the middle of next week, Weather Services Corp said.
Separately, testing of a possible gas leak was in progress in Louisiana's Vermilion Bay, the Coast Guard said, but no further details were yet available.
